chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:
My father would perform Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, from the door of Ibn 'Abbad until he raised his feet from the mile marker, not reaching the alley of the family of Abu Husayn.
And the Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah is a mandatory duty; this was narrated.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific boundaries for the Sa'i ritual between Safa and Marwah according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies the precise geographical limits of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir’s (peace be upon him) Sa'i, extending from the door of Ibn Abbad to the point where his feet left the Milestone (al-Mil), thereby establishing a scholarly precedent for the minimum valid distance. This narration underscores the practical application of the ritual within the confines of the Haram, reinforcing the obligation (fard) of Sa'i as a fundamental pillar of Hajj and Umrah.
